section_1.title: The Smoothie Analogy (Introduction)
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie is made of individual fruits, a complex signal is made of simple sine waves. The Fourier Transform is the tool that gives us the 'recipe'.
section_1.example: Chef Fourier blends a 'Sound Smoothie'. We see a messy, purple wave on a screen. He explains that we need to find out exactly how much banana (Frequency A) and how much blueberry (Frequency B) is inside.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Circle-Wave Connection
section_2.content: Explain that every pure sine wave can be visualized as a point moving around a circle at a constant speed. This establishes the relationship between rotation, frequency, and time.
section_2.example: A mechanical cat is sitting on a spinning Ferris wheel. A light shines from the side, projecting the cat's shadow onto a moving wall. The shadow traces a perfect, smooth sine wave.

section_3.title: The Messy Signal (Superposition)
section_3.content: Demonstrate that complex, 'ugly' waves are just multiple simple waves added together. This is the 'Time Domain' view.
section_3.example: We overlay three cats on three different Ferris wheels spinning at different speeds. When we sum their heights, the resulting 'Time Domain' wave looks like chaotic noise.

section_4.title: The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)
section_4.content: Introduce the concept of wrapping the complex signal around a circle at a variable 'winding frequency'. This is the visual representation of the Fourier integral.
section_4.example: Visualize the complex signal as a flexible wire. We wrap this wire around a spool that spins at a frequency 'f'. When 'f' matches one of the hidden 'ingredients' (frequencies), the shape on the spool becomes unbalanced.

section_5.title: The Center of Mass (The Peak)
section_5.content: Explain how to identify the hidden frequencies. When the winding frequency matches a component frequency, the 'center of mass' of the wrapped wire shifts away from the center of the circle.
section_5.example: A small yellow dot represents the center of mass. As the winding frequency changes, the dot stays near the center—until it suddenly 'jumps' outward when a hidden frequency is hit. This jump creates a spike on our graph.

section_6.title: The Frequency Domain (The Result)
section_6.content: Transition from the Time Domain (signal over time) to the Frequency Domain (strength at each frequency). This is the final Fourier Transform output.
section_6.example: The camera pans from the 'Time' view to a 'Frequency' view. We see three distinct vertical bars (spikes) corresponding to our three cats, showing exactly how fast each cat was spinning.

section_7.title: Real-World Application: Noise Cancellation
section_7.content: Show how this math is used in modern devices to filter unwanted noise by identifying and removing specific frequency spikes.
section_7.example: A character wearing noise-canceling headphones. The 'Fourier Robot' identifies a constant low-frequency spike caused by an airplane engine and digitally 'plucks' it out of the recipe, leaving only the music.

section_1.title: The Smoothie Analogy (Introduction)
lecture_lines: Complex signals are like smoothies made of many ingredients.
Individual ingredients are simple, repeating sine waves.
Fourier Transforms reveal the exact recipe for any signal.
animations: Show a purple smoothie cup icon (#9B59B6) in the center.
Fade in a chaotic purple waveform (#9B59B6) above the cup.
Icons of a Banana (#F1C40F) and Blueberry (#3498DB) slide in from the sides.
The chaotic wave splits into a Yellow sine wave (#F1C40F) and a Blue sine wave (#3498DB).
Display labels 'Banana: 440Hz' and 'Blueberry: 523Hz' next to the waves.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Circle-Wave Connection
lecture_lines: Every sine wave correlates to circular motion.
Imagine a point spinning around a circle at constant speed.
Tracking the vertical height over time creates a wave.
animations: Draw a white circle (#FFFFFF) on the left with a rotating dot.
A red line (#E74C3C) extends from the dot's height to the right.
The moving line traces a smooth red sine wave as the dot rotates.

section_3.title: The Messy Signal (Superposition)
lecture_lines: Real-world signals combine multiple sine waves together.
Summing different frequencies creates a messy, complex wave.
This "Time Domain" view hides the individual components.
animations: Stack three sine waves vertically: Red (#E74C3C), Green (#2ECC71), and Blue (#3498DB).
The three waves move towards each other and sum into one white wave (#ECF0F1).
Label the result 'Time Domain' at the bottom center.

section_4.title: The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)
lecture_lines: We wrap our complex signal around a central point.
The wrapping speed depends on a specific "winding frequency."
Most winding frequencies result in a balanced, circular mess.
But certain frequencies create a distinct, lopsided shape.
This happens when the winding matches a hidden component.
animations: Represent the complex white signal as a horizontal wire (#ECF0F1).
Wrap the wire around a central point to form a spiral.
Increase the wrapping speed, showing the spiral changing shape.
At a specific speed, the spiral becomes heavily offset to one side.
The lopsided spiral flashes Yellow (#F1C40F) to indicate a match.

section_5.title: The Center of Mass (The Peak)
lecture_lines: Think of the wrapped signal as a physical wire.
We calculate its center of mass as we spin.
Usually, the center of mass stays near the origin.
When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward.
This sudden "peak" signals we found an ingredient.
animations: Place a small yellow dot (#F1C40F) at the center of the wrapping shape.
Animate the dot vibrating near the center as wrapping frequency varies.
At the matching frequency, the dot jumps far to the right side.

section_6.title: The Frequency Domain (The Result)
lecture_lines: We plot these center-of-mass peaks on a new graph.
This is the "Frequency Domain" view of our signal.
Every peak represents one pure sine wave ingredient.
The horizontal position tells us the ingredient's frequency.
We have successfully decoded the signal's original recipe.
animations: Fade out the winding machine and fade in a horizontal frequency axis.
Three vertical spikes (Red, Green, Blue) grow at specific points on the axis.
Label the axis 'Frequency Domain' with white text.
Show the original fruit icons (Banana, Blueberry) above their respective spikes.
The spikes pulse to emphasize the final 'recipe' result.

section_7.title: Real-World Application: Noise Cancellation
lecture_lines: Noise cancellation uses this recipe to identify unwanted sounds.
Computers pluck out the specific frequencies causing noise.
The result is pure music without the background hum.
animations: Show a frequency plot with three clean spikes and many small grey spikes (#95A5A6).
A 'selector' box highlights the grey noise spikes.
The grey spikes vanish, leaving only the clean component spikes.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.9  # Adjusted x-offset to fit grid on the right side
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        PURPLE = "#9B59B6"
        YELLOW = "#F1C40F"
        BLUE = "#3498DB"

        title = "The Smoothie Analogy (Introduction)"
        lines = [
            "Complex signals are like smoothies made of many ingredients.",
            "Individual ingredients are simple, repeating sine waves.",
            "Fourier Transforms reveal the exact recipe for any signal."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(PURPLE)
        
        # Smoothie cup icon (Placeholder as a colored rectangle with rounded corners)
        smoothie_cup = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=1.5, width=1.0, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(smoothie_cup, "C3", "D4")
        
        # Chaotic purple waveform
        # f(x) = sin(2x) + 0.5sin(5x) + 0.2sin(10x)
        chaotic_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=PURPLE
        )
        self.place_in_area(chaotic_wave, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(smoothie_cup), Create(chaotic_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW) # We'll highlight with Yellow for the first ingredient
        
        # Fruit icons (Placeholders)
        banana_icon = Text("🍌", font_size=36) # Using emoji as placeholder icon
        self.place_at_grid(banana_icon, "A1")
        
        blueberry_icon = Text("🫐", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(blueberry_icon, "A6")
        
        # Split waves
        yellow_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_in_area(yellow_wave, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        blue_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(5 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=BLUE
        )
        self.place_in_area(blue_wave, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(banana_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(blueberry_icon, shift=LEFT),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE) # Transition color for the second ingredient
        )
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(chaotic_wave.copy(), yellow_wave),
            ReplacementTransform(chaotic_wave.copy(), blue_wave),

        # Data from shared state

        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of the wrapped signal as a physical wire.",
            "We calculate its center of mass as we spin.",
            "Usually, the center of mass stays near the origin.",
            "When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward.",

        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Create a complex winding wire (balanced state)

        def get_wrapped_wire(offset=0, freq_mod=1.0):

                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.cos(t) + offset,
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.sin(t),

        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(

            ]),
            t_range=[0, 2 * PI],
            color=COLOR_WIRE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(unbalanced_wire, CENTER_POS, scale_factor=0.6)

            rate_func=slow_into
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        )

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We wrap our complex signal around a central point.",
            "The wrapping speed depends on a specific \"winding frequency.\"",
            "Most winding frequencies result in a balanced, circular mess.",
            "But certain frequencies create a distinct, lopsided shape.",
            "This happens when the winding matches a hidden component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        WIRE_COLOR = "#ECF0F1"
        MATCH_COLOR = "#F1C40F"

        # Signal function: 1.4 + 0.6*cos(2*pi*2*t)
        # This signal has a component at 2.0 Hz.
        def signal_func(t):
            return 1.4 + 0.6 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * 2.0 * t)

        def get_wrapped_points(f, t_max=4.0, step=0.01):

                # Clockwise winding is the convention for Fourier transforms (e^-iwt)

                pts.append([r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), 0])
            return pts

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Wrap the wire around a central point to form a spiral.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        f_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        
        # Target wrapped wire starting shape
        wrapped_pts_start = get_wrapped_points(f_tracker.get_value())
        scaled_wrapped_pts_start = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in wrapped_pts_start]
        
        wrapped_wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wrapped_wire.set_points_as_corners(scaled_wrapped_pts_start)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wire, wrapped_wire))

            f = f_tracker.get_value()

            # Apply fixed scaling and center shift

            mob.set_points_as_corners(new_pts)

        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # At a specific speed, the spiral becomes heavily offset to one side.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Move towards the matching frequency (2.0 Hz)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The lopsided spiral flashes Yellow (#F1C40F) to indicate a match.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(MATCH_COLOR)
        
        # Pause updater to perform discrete flash animation
        wrapped_wire.remove_updater(wire_updater)
        
        # Successive flash pulses
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR).set_stroke(width=8),
                run_time=0.4
            )
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(WIRE_COLOR).set_stroke(width=4),
                run_time=0.4
            )
        
        # Final color set to Yellow
        self.play(wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR), run_time=0.3)

text_parts:
I have completed the Manim code for **Section 6: The Frequency Domain (The Result)**. 

The implementation follows the specified 6x6 grid system and uses the `TeachingScene` base class. Key features of this section include:
- **Transition Animation**: Fades out a placeholder winding machine while introducing the horizontal frequency axis.
- **Frequency Axis**: A clear horizontal axis at row D with "Frequency" and "Frequency Domain" labels.
- **Spectrum Visualization**: Three color-coded spikes (Red, Green, Blue) grow from the axis at distinct frequency points (2Hz, 5Hz, 8Hz).
- **Ingredient Decoding**: "Strawberry", "Banana", and "Blueberry" labels are positioned above their respective peaks to visually connect the frequencies back to the "smoothie recipe" analogy introduced earlier.
- **Pulsing Finale**: The spikes pulse to emphasize the successful decoding of the signal.

All lecture lines are highlighted sequentially in colors (White, Yellow, Red, Green, Blue) to match the on-screen animations.

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        title = "The Frequency Domain (The Result)"
        lines = [
            "We plot these center-of-mass peaks on a new graph.",
            "This is the \"Frequency Domain\" view of our signal.",
            "Every peak represents one pure sine wave ingredient.",
            "The horizontal position tells us the ingredient's frequency.",
            "We have successfully decoded the signal's original recipe."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors for highlights
        colors = [WHITE, YELLOW, RED, GREEN, BLUE]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade out the winding machine and fade in a horizontal frequency axis.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Placeholder for previous winding machine
        winding_machine = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.7, color=GREY, stroke_width=2, fill_opacity=0.2),
            Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color=GREY),
            Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=GREY)
        )
        self.place_in_area(winding_machine, "B2", "D5")
        self.add(winding_machine)
        
        # Frequency Axis (placed along row D)
        axis = Arrow(start=self.grid['D1'], end=self.grid['D6'], color=WHITE, buff=0)
        axis_label = Text("Frequency", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(axis_label, "F2", "F5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(winding_machine),
            Create(axis), 
            Write(axis_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Label the axis 'Frequency Domain' with white text.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        
        domain_label = Text("Frequency Domain", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(domain_label, "A2", "A5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(domain_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Three vertical spikes (Red, Green, Blue) grow at specific points on the axis.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        
        # Spikes: Red (2 units tall), Green (1.5 units), Blue (1 unit)
        spike_r = Line(self.grid['D2'], self.grid['B2'], color=RED, stroke_width=8)
        # For Green, we want it between B and C
        spike_g_top = (self.grid['B4'] + self.grid['C4']) / 2
        spike_g = Line(self.grid['D4'], spike_g_top, color=GREEN, stroke_width=8)
        spike_b = Line(self.grid['D6'], self.grid['C6'], color=BLUE, stroke_width=8)
        
        self.play(
            GrowFromEdge(spike_r, DOWN),
            GrowFromEdge(spike_g, DOWN),
            GrowFromEdge(spike_b, DOWN),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show the original fruit icons (Banana, Blueberry) above their respective spikes.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        
        # Fruits as text labels
        fruit1 = Text("Strawberry", color=RED, font_size=18)
        fruit2 = Text("Banana", color=GREEN, font_size=18)
        fruit3 = Text("Blueberry", color=BLUE, font_size=18)
        
        self.place_at_grid(fruit1, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(fruit2, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(fruit3, "B6")

        # Frequency values (2Hz, 5Hz, 8Hz) on row E
        freq1 = Text("2 Hz", font_size=16, color=RED)
        freq2 = Text("5 Hz", font_size=16, color=GREEN)
        freq3 = Text("8 Hz", font_size=16, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(freq1, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(freq2, "E4")
        self.place_at_grid(freq3, "E6")

        self.play(
            FadeIn(fruit1), FadeIn(fruit2), FadeIn(fruit3),
            Write(freq1), Write(freq2), Write(freq3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The spikes pulse to emphasize the final 'recipe' result.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        pulse_r = spike_r.animate.scale(1.1, about_point=self.grid['D2'])
        pulse_g = spike_g.animate.scale(1.1, about_point=self.grid['D4'])
        pulse_b = spike_b.animate.scale(1.1, about_point=self.grid['D6'])
        
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(pulse_r, pulse_g, pulse_b, rate_func=there_and_back, run_time=0.8)
        
        self.wait(3)
```

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        PURPLE = "#9B59B6"
        YELLOW = "#F1C40F"
        BLUE = "#3498DB"

        title = "The Smoothie Analogy (Introduction)"
        lines = [
            "Complex signals are like smoothies made of many ingredients.",
            "Individual ingredients are simple, repeating sine waves.",
            "Fourier Transforms reveal the exact recipe for any signal."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(PURPLE)
        
        # Smoothie cup icon (Placeholder as a colored rectangle with rounded corners)
        smoothie_cup = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=1.5, width=1.0, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(smoothie_cup, "C3", "D4")
        
        # Chaotic purple waveform
        # f(x) = sin(2x) + 0.5sin(5x) + 0.2sin(10x)
        chaotic_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=PURPLE
        )
        self.place_in_area(chaotic_wave, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(smoothie_cup), Create(chaotic_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW) # We'll highlight with Yellow for the first ingredient
        
        # Fruit icons (Placeholders)
        banana_icon = Text("🍌", font_size=36) # Using emoji as placeholder icon
        self.place_at_grid(banana_icon, "A1")
        
        blueberry_icon = Text("🫐", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(blueberry_icon, "A6")
        
        # Split waves
        yellow_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_in_area(yellow_wave, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        blue_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(5 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=BLUE
        )
        self.place_in_area(blue_wave, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(banana_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(blueberry_icon, shift=LEFT),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE) # Transition color for the second ingredient
        )
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(chaotic_wave.copy(), yellow_wave),
            ReplacementTransform(chaotic_wave.copy(), blue_wave),
            chaotic_wave.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE) # Reveal the recipe
        
        banana_label = Text("Banana: 440Hz", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(banana_label, "D2")
        
        blueberry_label = Text("Blueberry: 523Hz", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(blueberry_label, "F2")
        
        self.play(
            Write(banana_label),
            Write(blueberry_label),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Circle-Wave Connection"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Every sine wave correlates to circular motion.",
            "- Imagine a point spinning around a circle at constant speed.",
            "- Tracking the vertical height over time creates a wave."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CIRCLE = WHITE
        COLOR_WAVE = "#E74C3C"  # Red

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every sine wave correlates to circular motion.
        # Draw a white circle (#FFFFFF) on the left with a rotating dot.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CIRCLE)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.2, color=COLOR_CIRCLE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "C2")
        
        dot_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot = Dot(color=COLOR_CIRCLE)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            circle.get_center() + circle.radius * np.array([np.cos(dot_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(dot_tracker.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(circle), FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Imagine a point spinning around a circle at constant speed.
        # A red line (#E74C3C) extends from the dot's height to the right.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_WAVE)

        # Horizontal line connecting dot to the wave starting point
        # The wave starts at grid C4
        wave_start_x = self.grid["C4"][0]
        
        connection_line = Line(
            start=dot.get_center(),
            end=[wave_start_x, dot.get_center()[1], 0],
            color=COLOR_WAVE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        connection_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            dot.get_center(),
            [wave_start_x, dot.get_center()[1], 0]
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(connection_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Tracking the vertical height over time creates a wave.
        # The moving line traces a smooth red sine wave as the dot rotates.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_WAVE)

        # We trace the point at the end of the connection line as it moves right
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        tracing_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_WAVE, radius=0.01) # Invisible point to trace
        
        # The tracing dot moves horizontally to the right while its Y matches the dot
        # We'll use a TracedPath for the wave
        tracing_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            [wave_start_x + time_tracker.get_value() * 1.5, dot.get_center()[1], 0]
        ))
        
        wave_path = TracedPath(tracing_dot.get_center, stroke_color=COLOR_WAVE, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.add(tracing_dot, wave_path)
        
        # Animate the rotation and the wave tracing
        # Rotate for two full cycles
        self.play(
            dot_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI),
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(2),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We wrap our complex signal around a central point.",
            "The wrapping speed depends on a specific \"winding frequency.\"",
            "Most winding frequencies result in a balanced, circular mess.",
            "But certain frequencies create a distinct, lopsided shape.",
            "This happens when the winding matches a hidden component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        WIRE_COLOR = "#ECF0F1"
        MATCH_COLOR = "#F1C40F"

        # Signal function: 1.4 + 0.6*cos(2*pi*2*t)
        # This signal has a component at 2.0 Hz.
        def signal_func(t):
            return 1.4 + 0.6 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * 2.0 * t)

        def get_wrapped_points(f, t_max=4.0, step=0.01):
            pts = []
            for t in np.arange(0, t_max + step, step):
                r = signal_func(t)
                # Clockwise winding is the convention for Fourier transforms (e^-iwt)
                theta = -2 * np.pi * f * t
                pts.append([r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), 0])
            return pts

        # Area center for wrapping machine
        tl = self.grid["B2"]
        br = self.grid["E5"]
        area_center = (tl + br) / 2
        # Radius of signal is approx 2.0. Area height/width is 3.0.
        # Scale by 0.6 means signal fits in 2.0 * 0.6 * 2 = 2.4 units.
        SCALE = 0.6

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent the complex white signal as a horizontal wire (#ECF0F1).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Initial wire: horizontal representation of the signal values
        wire_pts = [ [ (t - 2.0) * 0.8, (signal_func(t) - 1.4) * 1.5, 0] for t in np.arange(0, 4.01, 0.05) ]
        wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wire.set_points_as_corners(wire_pts)
        self.place_in_area(wire, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(wire))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Wrap the wire around a central point to form a spiral.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        f_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        
        # Target wrapped wire starting shape
        wrapped_pts_start = get_wrapped_points(f_tracker.get_value())
        scaled_wrapped_pts_start = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in wrapped_pts_start]
        
        wrapped_wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wrapped_wire.set_points_as_corners(scaled_wrapped_pts_start)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wire, wrapped_wire))
        
        # Updater for winding frequency based on tracker
        def wire_updater(mob):
            f = f_tracker.get_value()
            pts = get_wrapped_points(f)
            # Apply fixed scaling and center shift
            new_pts = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in pts]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(new_pts)

        wrapped_wire.add_updater(wire_updater)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Increase the wrapping speed, showing the spiral changing shape.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Sweep through non-matching frequencies (balanced/circular mess)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(0.7), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # At a specific speed, the spiral becomes heavily offset to one side.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Move towards the matching frequency (2.0 Hz)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The lopsided spiral flashes Yellow (#F1C40F) to indicate a match.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(MATCH_COLOR)
        
        # Pause updater to perform discrete flash animation
        wrapped_wire.remove_updater(wire_updater)
        
        # Successive flash pulses
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR).set_stroke(width=8),
                run_time=0.4
            )
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(WIRE_COLOR).set_stroke(width=4),
                run_time=0.4
            )
        
        # Final color set to Yellow
        self.play(wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "The Center of Mass (The Peak)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of the wrapped signal as a physical wire.",
            "We calculate its center of mass as we spin.",
            "Usually, the center of mass stays near the origin.",
            "When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward.",
            "This sudden \"peak\" signals we found an ingredient."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_WIRE = "#ECF0F1"  # White wire
        COLOR_DOT = "#F1C40F"   # Yellow center of mass dot
        
        # Grid positions
        CENTER_POS = "D3"
        RIGHT_POS = "D5"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Think of the wrapped signal as a physical wire."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a complex winding wire (balanced state)
        # Using a parametric function to simulate a wrapped signal
        def get_wrapped_wire(offset=0, freq_mod=1.0):
            return ParametricFunction(
                lambda t: np.array([
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.cos(t) + offset,
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.sin(t),
                    0
                ]),
                t_range=[0, 2 * PI],
                color=COLOR_WIRE
            )
            
        wire = get_wrapped_wire()
        self.place_at_grid(wire, CENTER_POS, scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(wire))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We calculate its center of mass as we spin."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation 1: Place a small yellow dot at the center
        dot = Dot(color=COLOR_DOT, radius=0.08)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, CENTER_POS)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot, scale=0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Usually, the center of mass stays near the origin."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation 2: Animate the dot vibrating near the center
        # We use a ValueTracker to jitter the dot
        jitter_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            self.grid[CENTER_POS] + 
            np.array([0.1 * np.sin(jitter_tracker.get_value() * 10), 
                      0.1 * np.cos(jitter_tracker.get_value() * 7), 
                      0])
        ))
        
        self.play(jitter_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation 3: At the matching frequency, the dot jumps far to the right side.
        # First, prepare the "unbalanced" wire
        unbalanced_wire = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                (1.5 + 1.2 * np.cos(t)) * np.cos(t), # Lopsided towards positive x
                (1.5 + 1.2 * np.cos(t)) * np.sin(t),
                0
            ]),
            t_range=[0, 2 * PI],
            color=COLOR_WIRE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(unbalanced_wire, CENTER_POS, scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Stop the jitter updater before the jump
        dot.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            Transform(wire, unbalanced_wire),
            dot.animate.move_to(self.grid[RIGHT_POS]),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This sudden 'peak' signals we found an ingredient."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pulse the dot to emphasize the "peak"
        self.play(
            dot.animate.scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE),
            Flash(self.grid[RIGHT_POS], color=COLOR_DOT, line_length=0.3, num_lines=8),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            dot.animate.scale(1/1.5).set_color(COLOR_DOT),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for final state
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        title = "The Frequency Domain (The Result)"
        lines = [
            "We plot these center-of-mass peaks on a new graph.",
            "This is the \"Frequency Domain\" view of our signal.",
            "Every peak represents one pure sine wave ingredient.",
            "The horizontal position tells us the ingredient's frequency.",
            "We have successfully decoded the signal's original recipe."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors for highlights
        colors = [WHITE, YELLOW, RED, GREEN, BLUE]

        self.place_at_grid(fruit3, "B6")

            Write(freq1), Write(freq2), Write(freq3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The spikes pulse to emphasize the final 'recipe' result.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        pulse_r = spike_r.animate.scale(1.1, about_point=self.grid['D2'])
        pulse_g = spike_g.animate.scale(1.1, about_point=self.grid['D4'])
        pulse_b = spike_b.animate.scale(1.1, about_point=self.grid['D6'])
        
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(pulse_r, pulse_g, pulse_b, rate_func=there_and_back, run_time=0.8)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We wrap our complex signal around a central point.",
            "The wrapping speed depends on a specific \"winding frequency.\"",
            "Most winding frequencies result in a balanced, circular mess.",
            "But certain frequencies create a distinct, lopsided shape.",
            "This happens when the winding matches a hidden component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        WIRE_COLOR = "#ECF0F1"
        MATCH_COLOR = "#F1C40F"

        # Signal function: 1.4 + 0.6*cos(2*pi*2*t)
        # This signal has a component at 2.0 Hz.
        def signal_func(t):
            return 1.4 + 0.6 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * 2.0 * t)

        def get_wrapped_points(f, t_max=4.0, step=0.01):
            pts = []
            for t in np.arange(0, t_max + step, step):
                r = signal_func(t)
                # Clockwise winding is the convention for Fourier transforms (e^-iwt)
                theta = -2 * np.pi * f * t
                pts.append([r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), 0])
            return pts

        # Area center for wrapping machine
        tl = self.grid["B2"]
        br = self.grid["E5"]
        area_center = (tl + br) / 2
        # Radius of signal is approx 2.0. Area height/width is 3.0.
        # Scale by 0.6 means signal fits in 2.0 * 0.6 * 2 = 2.4 units.
        SCALE = 0.6

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent the complex white signal as a horizontal wire (#ECF0F1).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Initial wire: horizontal representation of the signal values
        wire_pts = [ [ (t - 2.0) * 0.8, (signal_func(t) - 1.4) * 1.5, 0] for t in np.arange(0, 4.01, 0.05) ]
        wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wire.set_points_as_corners(wire_pts)
        self.place_in_area(wire, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(wire))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Wrap the wire around a central point to form a spiral.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        f_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        
        # Target wrapped wire starting shape
        wrapped_pts_start = get_wrapped_points(f_tracker.get_value())
        scaled_wrapped_pts_start = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in wrapped_pts_start]
        
        wrapped_wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wrapped_wire.set_points_as_corners(scaled_wrapped_pts_start)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wire, wrapped_wire))
        
        # Updater for winding frequency based on tracker
        def wire_updater(mob):
            f = f_tracker.get_value()
            pts = get_wrapped_points(f)
            # Apply fixed scaling and center shift
            new_pts = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in pts]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(new_pts)

        wrapped_wire.add_updater(wire_updater)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Increase the wrapping speed, showing the spiral changing shape.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Sweep through non-matching frequencies (balanced/circular mess)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(0.7), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # At a specific speed, the spiral becomes heavily offset to one side.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Move towards the matching frequency (2.0 Hz)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The lopsided spiral flashes Yellow (#F1C40F) to indicate a match.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(MATCH_COLOR)
        
        # Pause updater to perform discrete flash animation
        wrapped_wire.remove_updater(wire_updater)
        
        # Successive flash pulses
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR).set_stroke(width=8),
                run_time=0.4
            )
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(WIRE_COLOR).set_stroke(width=4),
                run_time=0.4
            )
        
        # Final color set to Yellow
        self.play(wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        PURPLE = "#9B59B6"
        YELLOW = "#F1C40F"
        BLUE = "#3498DB"

        title = "The Smoothie Analogy (Introduction)"
        lines = [
            "Complex signals are like smoothies made of many ingredients.",
            "Individual ingredients are simple, repeating sine waves.",
            "Fourier Transforms reveal the exact recipe for any signal."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(PURPLE)
        
        # Smoothie cup icon (Placeholder as a colored rectangle with rounded corners)
        smoothie_cup = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=1.5, width=1.0, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(smoothie_cup, "C3", "D4")
        
        # Chaotic purple waveform
        # f(x) = sin(2x) + 0.5sin(5x) + 0.2sin(10x)
        chaotic_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=PURPLE
        )
        self.place_in_area(chaotic_wave, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(smoothie_cup), Create(chaotic_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW) # We'll highlight with Yellow for the first ingredient
        
        # Fruit icons (Placeholders)
        banana_icon = Text("🍌", font_size=36) # Using emoji as placeholder icon
        self.place_at_grid(banana_icon, "A1")
        
        blueberry_icon = Text("🫐", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(blueberry_icon, "A6")
        
        # Split waves
        yellow_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_in_area(yellow_wave, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        blue_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(5 * x),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=BLUE
        )
        self.place_in_area(blue_wave, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(banana_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            FadeIn(blueberry_icon, shift=LEFT),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE) # Transition color for the second ingredient
        )
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(chaotic_wave.copy(), yellow_wave),
            ReplacementTransform(chaotic_wave.copy(), blue_wave),
            chaotic_wave.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE) # Reveal the recipe
        
        banana_label = Text("Banana: 440Hz", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(banana_label, "D2")
        
        blueberry_label = Text("Blueberry: 523Hz", font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(blueberry_label, "F2")
        
        self.play(
            Write(banana_label),
            Write(blueberry_label),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE)
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Circle-Wave Connection"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Every sine wave correlates to circular motion.",
            "- Imagine a point spinning around a circle at constant speed.",
            "- Tracking the vertical height over time creates a wave."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_CIRCLE = WHITE
        COLOR_WAVE = "#E74C3C"  # Red

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every sine wave correlates to circular motion.
        # Draw a white circle (#FFFFFF) on the left with a rotating dot.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CIRCLE)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.2, color=COLOR_CIRCLE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "C2")
        
        dot_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot = Dot(color=COLOR_CIRCLE)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            circle.get_center() + circle.radius * np.array([np.cos(dot_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(dot_tracker.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(circle), FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Imagine a point spinning around a circle at constant speed.
        # A red line (#E74C3C) extends from the dot's height to the right.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_WAVE)

        # Horizontal line connecting dot to the wave starting point
        # The wave starts at grid C4
        wave_start_x = self.grid["C4"][0]
        
        connection_line = Line(
            start=dot.get_center(),
            end=[wave_start_x, dot.get_center()[1], 0],
            color=COLOR_WAVE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        connection_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(
            dot.get_center(),
            [wave_start_x, dot.get_center()[1], 0]
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(connection_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Tracking the vertical height over time creates a wave.
        # The moving line traces a smooth red sine wave as the dot rotates.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_WAVE)

        # We trace the point at the end of the connection line as it moves right
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        tracing_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_WAVE, radius=0.01) # Invisible point to trace
        
        # The tracing dot moves horizontally to the right while its Y matches the dot
        # We'll use a TracedPath for the wave
        tracing_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            [wave_start_x + time_tracker.get_value() * 1.5, dot.get_center()[1], 0]
        ))
        
        wave_path = TracedPath(tracing_dot.get_center, stroke_color=COLOR_WAVE, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.add(tracing_dot, wave_path)
        
        # Animate the rotation and the wave tracing
        # Rotate for two full cycles
        self.play(
            dot_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI),
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(2),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "The Center of Mass (The Peak)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of the wrapped signal as a physical wire.",
            "We calculate its center of mass as we spin.",
            "Usually, the center of mass stays near the origin.",
            "When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward.",
            "This sudden \"peak\" signals we found an ingredient."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_WIRE = "#ECF0F1"  # White wire
        COLOR_DOT = "#F1C40F"   # Yellow center of mass dot
        
        # Grid positions
        CENTER_POS = "D3"
        RIGHT_POS = "D5"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Think of the wrapped signal as a physical wire."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a complex winding wire (balanced state)
        # Using a parametric function to simulate a wrapped signal
        def get_wrapped_wire(offset=0, freq_mod=1.0):
            return ParametricFunction(
                lambda t: np.array([
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.cos(t) + offset,
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.sin(t),
                    0
                ]),
                t_range=[0, 2 * PI],
                color=COLOR_WIRE
            )
            
        wire = get_wrapped_wire()
        self.place_at_grid(wire, CENTER_POS, scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(wire))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "We calculate its center of mass as we spin."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation 1: Place a small yellow dot at the center
        dot = Dot(color=COLOR_DOT, radius=0.08)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, CENTER_POS)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot, scale=0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Usually, the center of mass stays near the origin."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation 2: Animate the dot vibrating near the center
        # We use a ValueTracker to jitter the dot
        jitter_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            self.grid[CENTER_POS] + 
            np.array([0.1 * np.sin(jitter_tracker.get_value() * 10), 
                      0.1 * np.cos(jitter_tracker.get_value() * 7), 
                      0])
        ))
        
        self.play(jitter_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animation 3: At the matching frequency, the dot jumps far to the right side.
        # First, prepare the "unbalanced" wire
        unbalanced_wire = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([
                (1.5 + 1.2 * np.cos(t)) * np.cos(t), # Lopsided towards positive x
                (1.5 + 1.2 * np.cos(t)) * np.sin(t),
                0
            ]),
            t_range=[0, 2 * PI],
            color=COLOR_WIRE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(unbalanced_wire, CENTER_POS, scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Stop the jitter updater before the jump
        dot.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            Transform(wire, unbalanced_wire),
            dot.animate.move_to(self.grid[RIGHT_POS]),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "This sudden 'peak' signals we found an ingredient."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pulse the dot to emphasize the "peak"
        self.play(
            dot.animate.scale(1.5).set_color(WHITE),
            Flash(self.grid[RIGHT_POS], color=COLOR_DOT, line_length=0.3, num_lines=8),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            dot.animate.scale(1/1.5).set_color(COLOR_DOT),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset colors for final state
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

            "When we hit a hidden frequency, it jumps outward.",

                lambda t: np.array([
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.cos(t),
                    (1.5 + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * t * freq_mod)) * np.sin(t),

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            time_tracker.animate.set_value(2.5),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We wrap our complex signal around a central point.",
            "The wrapping speed depends on a specific \"winding frequency.\"",
            "Most winding frequencies result in a balanced, circular mess.",
            "But certain frequencies create a distinct, lopsided shape.",
            "This happens when the winding matches a hidden component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        WIRE_COLOR = "#ECF0F1"
        MATCH_COLOR = "#F1C40F"

        # Signal function: 1.4 + 0.6*cos(2*pi*2*t)
        # This signal has a component at 2.0 Hz.
        def signal_func(t):
            return 1.4 + 0.6 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * 2.0 * t)

        def get_wrapped_points(f, t_max=4.0, step=0.01):
            pts = []
            for t in np.arange(0, t_max + step, step):
                r = signal_func(t)
                # Clockwise winding is the convention for Fourier transforms (e^-iwt)
                theta = -2 * np.pi * f * t
                pts.append([r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), 0])
            return pts

        # Area center for wrapping machine (using B1 to F6 as per Issue 53 fix)
        tl_pos = self.grid["B1"]
        br_pos = self.grid["F6"]

        # Apply fix from Issue 53: place in B1-F6 with scale 0.9
        self.place_in_area(wire, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)

        wrapped_pts_start = get_wrapped_points(f_tracker.get_value())
        scaled_wrapped_pts_start = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in wrapped_pts_start]

        def wire_updater(mob):
            f = f_tracker.get_value()
            pts = get_wrapped_points(f)
            # Apply fixed scaling and center shift
            new_pts = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in pts]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(new_pts)

        wrapped_wire.add_updater(wire_updater)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Increase the wrapping speed, showing the spiral changing shape.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)

        self.wait(2)

        # The lopsided spiral flashes Yellow (#F1C40F) to indicate a match.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(MATCH_COLOR)
        
        # Remove updater to perform discrete flash animation and avoid interference
        wrapped_wire.remove_updater(wire_updater)
        
        # Successive flash pulses
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR).set_stroke(width=8),
                run_time=0.4
            )

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Winding Machine (The Core Mechanism)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We wrap our complex signal around a central point.",
            "The wrapping speed depends on a specific \"winding frequency.\"",
            "Most winding frequencies result in a balanced, circular mess.",
            "But certain frequencies create a distinct, lopsided shape.",
            "This happens when the winding matches a hidden component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        WIRE_COLOR = "#ECF0F1"
        MATCH_COLOR = "#F1C40F"

        # Signal function: 1.4 + 0.6*cos(2*pi*2*t)
        # This signal has a component at 2.0 Hz.
        def signal_func(t):
            return 1.4 + 0.6 * np.cos(2 * np.pi * 2.0 * t)

        def get_wrapped_points(f, t_max=4.0, step=0.01):
            pts = []
            for t in np.arange(0, t_max + step, step):
                r = signal_func(t)
                # Clockwise winding is the convention for Fourier transforms (e^-iwt)
                theta = -2 * np.pi * f * t
                pts.append([r * np.cos(theta), r * np.sin(theta), 0])
            return pts

        # Area center for wrapping machine (using B1 to F6 as per Issue 53 fix)
        tl_pos = self.grid["B1"]
        br_pos = self.grid["F6"]
        area_center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        # Internal scaling factor for the spiral geometry
        SCALE = 0.55 

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Initial wire: horizontal representation of the signal values
        wire_pts = [ [ (t - 2.0) * 0.8, (signal_func(t) - 1.4) * 1.5, 0] for t in np.arange(0, 4.01, 0.05) ]
        wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wire.set_points_as_corners(wire_pts)
        # Apply fix from Issue 53: place in B1-F6 with scale 0.9
        self.place_in_area(wire, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(wire))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        f_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        wrapped_pts_start = get_wrapped_points(f_tracker.get_value())
        scaled_wrapped_pts_start = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in wrapped_pts_start]
        
        wrapped_wire = VMobject(color=WIRE_COLOR)
        wrapped_wire.set_points_as_corners(scaled_wrapped_pts_start)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wire, wrapped_wire))
        
        # Updater for winding frequency based on tracker
        def wire_updater(mob):
            f = f_tracker.get_value()
            pts = get_wrapped_points(f)
            new_pts = [np.array(p) * SCALE + area_center for p in pts]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(new_pts)

        wrapped_wire.add_updater(wire_updater)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Sweep through non-matching frequencies
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(0.7), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WIRE_COLOR)
        
        # Move towards the matching frequency (2.0 Hz)
        self.play(f_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(MATCH_COLOR)
        
        # Remove updater to perform discrete flash animation
        wrapped_wire.remove_updater(wire_updater)
        
        # Successive flash pulses to indicate a match
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR).set_stroke(width=8),
                run_time=0.4
            )
            self.play(
                wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(WIRE_COLOR).set_stroke(width=4),
                run_time=0.4
            )
        
        self.play(wrapped_wire.animate.set_color(MATCH_COLOR), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(2)
